fact: NatCA states that in November 2024 Sierra Leone and Guinea signed an agreement to interconnect their national internet backbone networks.

SOGEB (Guinea) and Leoncom (Sierra Leone) signed an interconnection agreement in Conakry to link their national fibre networks at Pamelap on the border, with initial capacity of 42.5 Gbps and plans for 100 Gbps by 2026; the document gives no date for the signing, so its published date is used.

The PeeringDB record of 3 June 2026, written by the operator Michcom Limited, describes Michcom-IX as an open exchange point serving Sierra Leone, Guinea and Liberia with points of presence in Freetown and Jui plus Guilab in Conakry and CCL in Monrovia; all five listed peers are Sierra Leone networks.
Michcom-IX says its open-access exchange is live with points of presence in Freetown, Jui, Conakry and Monrovia, interconnecting 15 networks across Sierra Leone, Guinea and Liberia.
